newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank earnings set record pace in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank earnings set record pace in 1996.

text.p: U.S. commercial banks generated a record $52.7 billion in net income during 1996, according to an estimate by SNL Securities, a firm that gathers data on the financial services industry.

SNL said that based on results posted by 140 early reporting banks that account for 76 percent of the industry's assets, the fourth quarter brought earnings of an estimated $13.7 billion, just $100 million beneath the all-time high posted during the third quarter of 1995.

"After recording charges in the third quarter for SAIF recapitalization, the banking industry now enjoys a stabilized quarterly earnings rate of just under $14 billion," said Reid Nagle, president of SNL Securities. "At this point, earnings growth is unlikely to exceed 5-6 percent per year and downside risk exists if either inflation heats up or credit quality deteriorates."
